218: Physical-line metadata conceptually includes:
219: 
220: - logical-Tag visibility (`tag_valid` or equivalent);
221: - physical data readiness state;
222: - reference count;
223: - merge/wakeup information for pending data.
224: 
225: A physical line is reclaimable only when:
226: 
227: `tag_valid == 0 && ref_count == 0`
228: 
229: A logical Tag replacement clears the old physical line's `tag_valid` but does not free it while references remain.
230: 
231: A ready PIB entry may retire out of program/FIFO order subject to the one-instruction-per-cycle retire bandwidth and any required architectural ordering constraints added in later stages.
232: 
233: ## 10. Ref Count — frozen granularity
234: 
235: The reproduction uses **per-coalesced-cacheline-reference** Ref Count semantics.
236: 
237: Definition:
238: 
239: > one coalesced **128B cacheline reference/request** held by a live PIB instruction contributes one reference to the referenced physical 128B line.
240: 
241: Consequences:
242: 
243: - multiple lanes coalesced into one 128B cacheline request contribute **+1**, not +N lanes;
244: - a fully divergent 32-thread warp can generate at most 32 distinct 128B cacheline references;
245: - OO PIB depth 128 gives the conservative upper bound `128 × 32 = 4096`, so the paper-compatible default Ref Count width is **13 bits**;
246: - Ref Count is a **physical-line-level** lifetime counter, not a sector-level counter;
247: - the corresponding reference is decremented when that PIB instruction releases/completes that coalesced line dependency according to the OO retirement semantics.
248: 
249: Do not reinterpret the counter as per-thread without a later explicit specification change.
250: 
251: ## 11. Pending-hit merging and lower-request identity
252: 
253: DTC must not rely on the traditional MSHR table for its own capacity/merge semantics.
254: 
255: While a logical tag maps to a physical line/sector already pending:
256: 
257: - a later coalesced request attaches to that pending physical allocation;
258: - it must not issue a duplicate lower request for the same pending data;
259: - completion wakes every attached dependency exactly once.
260: 
261: A Tag can later be evicted while an old physical allocation/request is still in flight. Therefore a lower-memory response must be associated with the intended **physical allocation identity**, not merely by re-looking up the current logical Tag address.
262: 
263: Implementation may use an existing request UID or an explicit `{phys_id, generation}`-style identity. Exact representation is an M1 implementation decision, but stale fills into a recycled physical line are forbidden.
264: 
265: ## 12. Whole-line paper mode
266: 
267: The primary reproduction of the thesis figures uses a **whole-line 128B DTC mode**:
268: 
269: - Tag→Physical renaming granularity: 128B;
270: - data INVALID/PENDING/VALID state granularity: 128B;
271: - fill/miss dependency granularity: 128B;
272: - Merge Mask/wakeup granularity: 128B.
273: 
274: This mode is the reference for paper-reproduction experiments and should be implemented/validated before the modern sector extension is treated as formal evidence.
275: 
276: ## 13. Modern sector extension
277: 
278: The modern Accel-Sim extension preserves the original renaming granularity while refining data readiness:
279: 
280: - Tag→Physical mapping remains **one 128B logical line → one 128B physical line**;
281: - physical line is divided into **4 × 32B sectors** for readiness;
282: - each sector has INVALID/PENDING/VALID state;
283: - OO Merge Mask/wakeup state is per sector;
284: - `wait_cnt` counts outstanding **sector dependencies**;
285: - Ref Count remains **line-level per coalesced 128B cacheline reference**, not per sector;
286: - one coalesced 128B line reference may carry a sector mask and still contributes only one line-level Ref Count increment;
287: - a physical line can be reclaimed only when line-level `tag_valid == 0` and line-level `ref_count == 0`.
